## Summary

> [!NOTE]
> Used agents to retrieve these possible perf findings

There are four commits in this PR, all of them aimed to incraese performance in some parts of the formatter. Some are directed to YAML, some are broader:

- [`13f799d` (this PR)](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/11613/changes/13f799d3d4b9fe3ccec2da850b8f4a961a8ce819) uses a slice method to avoid copying values
- [`0f9e357` (this PR)](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/11613/changes/0f9e357bae006761653d159388fb209e84570f7d) the indentations are emitted in bulk instead of calling `push_*` for each character
- [`f2c61d6` (this PR)](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/11613/changes/f2c61d656bce538ca1dd7a34edb970207c7134bc) avoid scanning scalar subtrees
- [`32a6f5c` (this PR)](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/11613/changes/32a6f5c8c0f1203f1e125b45fb6bf99af8809a7d) stores a small binary in the `GreenToken` that indicates whether the token has comments. issue.title: 💅 useNullishCoalescing is 3.81x slower in 2.5.12 on a Zod-inferred property

labels.name: repo-4d08208b
labels.description: Status: report has been confirmed as a valid bug

issue.body:
### Environment information

<details>

```text
CLI:
  Version: 2.5.12

Platform:
  CPU Architecture: aarch64
  OS: macos 27.0
  CPU: Apple M1 Max

Environment:
  BIOME_DISTRIBUTION: npm
  JS_RUNTIME_VERSION: v24.12.0
  JS_RUNTIME_NAME: node

Biome Configuration:
  Status: Loaded successfully
  Path: biome.json
  VCS enabled: false
  Enabled rule: nursery/useNullishCoalescing
```

</details>

### Rule name

`nursery/useNullishCoalescing`

### Playground link

https://github.com/jakeleventhal/biome-use-nullish-coalescing-perf-repro

The repository pins Biome 2.5.10 and 2.5.12 side by side. Run:

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run bench
bun run profile:2.5.10
bun run profile:2.5.12
```

The analyzed file contains one `||` expression whose left operand comes from a minimal Zod-inferred type:

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

const schema = z.object({
	state: z.string().max(100),
});

interface Request {
	body: z.infer<typeof schema>;
}

export function getOrderState(req: Request) {
	return req.body.state || null;
}
```

Five-run averages on the machine above:

| Version | End-to-end average | `useNullishCoalescing` rule time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2.5.10 | 1.499s | 1.397s |
| 2.5.12 | 5.529s | 5.317s |

That is a 3.69x end-to-end slowdown and a 3.81x increase inside the single rule invocation. Changing `||` to `??` reduces the 2.5.12 rule time to 1.459 microseconds.

### Expected result

Biome 2.5.12 should process this expression in roughly the same time as 2.5.10. `useNullishCoalescing` should not spend more than five seconds resolving a property from this minimal Zod-inferred type.

import type { UseFormReturn } from "react-hook-form";
import { z } from "zod";

const formSchema = z.object({
	ounces: z.number().nonnegative(),
	pounds: z.number().nonnegative(),
});

test<Context>(async (args) => {
    const service = args.service;
    service.go();
})

## Summary

Add a `noBunModules` lint rule as a counter rule to `noNodejsModules`.

The rule should report imports of Bun runtime built-in modules, including `bun:test`.

## Rationale

The current work adds support for resolving Bun built-in modules. Projects that do not target the Bun runtime need a rule that prevents Bun-specific imports.

## Affected areas

- JavaScript analyser lint rules in `crates/biome_js_analyze`
- Rule configuration and generated documentation
- Rule fixtures and snapshots

## Acceptance criteria

- Add and register a `noBunModules` rule.
- Report Bun built-in module imports, including `bun:test`.
- Include valid and invalid fixtures with reviewed snapshots.
- Generate the rule and configuration artefacts required for analyser rules.

issue.title: 2FA secret QR code for Bitwarden/KeePassXC needs to be Base32 encoded instead Base64
issue.body:
### Version

0.18.4

### What happened?

Use command `steamguard qr --format bitwarden` to generate 2FA secret QR code for Bitwarden to import as TOTP setup. Bitwarden accepted the secret, but the TOTP code it generates is always different with the one steamguard-cli generates. Of 'coz the code from Bitwarden won't work during login, while the one steamguard-cli generates is good.

Further investigation says that Bitwarden expects Base32 encoded but now it's Base64. Also the universal standard adopted across all modern password managers and authenticators (Bitwarden, 1Password, KeePassXC, Google Authenticator) is the [Google Authenticator Key-Uri-Format](https://github.com/google/google-authenticator/wiki/Key-Uri-Format#secret).
> The secret parameter is an arbitrary key value encoded in Base32 according to [RFC 3548](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3548). The padding specified in [RFC 3548 section 2.2](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3548#section-2.2) is not required and should be omitted.

I manually convert the 2FA secret within the string from Base64 to Base32, and it works fine this way.

Related to #502.

It's essentially:

- collect groups of referenced bindings from the binary expressions in the condition. for example, `foo < bar && baz !== qux` is 4 references, 2 groups of 2 references, `[foo, bar]` and `[baz, qux]`.

issue.title: Svelte: HTML comment inside a tag is accepted, but the file cannot compile

labels.name: repo-4d08208b
labels.description: Status: report has been confirmed as a valid bug

issue.body:
### Environment information

```
Biome 2.5.10
Windows 11, Node 22.14.0
Svelte 5.57.0
```

### Description

Biome accepts an HTML comment placed **inside** a Svelte tag, between attributes. Svelte rejects that markup outright, so `biome check` reports a clean file that cannot compile.

Since Svelte 5.53 a comment between attributes is valid — but only as a JS-style comment (`//` or `/* */`), which Biome already parses. The HTML form is not valid in any Svelte version.

This matters for suppression comments in particular. When a lint diagnostic points at an attribute inside a multi-line tag, `<!-- biome-ignore ... -->` looks like the natural place to put it, Biome silently accepts it, and the file only breaks later at build time.

### Steps to reproduce

`B.svelte`:

```svelte
<input
	type="text"
	<!-- a comment -->
	disabled
>
```

Run `biome check B.svelte`.

### Expected result

A parse error, the same way the Svelte compiler reports one:

```
expected_token — Expected token >
```

### Actual result

```
Checked 1 file in 1988µs. No fixes applied.
```

No diagnostic at all. `biome format` also reports nothing.

For comparison, `svelte.compile()` on the same source throws `expected_token`. The JS-style form in the same position compiles fine and Biome honours it as a suppression:

```svelte
<input
	type="text"
	// biome-ignore lint/a11y/noAutofocus: reason
	{autofocus}
>
```
